probe_history.reason:
The venue's own official calendar (https://www.radialsystem.de/en/programm/programm/) is fully server-rendered: every event card in the raw HTML carries a stable detail link (/en/veranstaltungen/{slug}/), a title (

...), one or more dateblocks (////time), a room (

), and a category tag. Alpine.js directives (x-show, @click) are present for interactive show/hide filtering only -- the underlying data is already in the raw HTML, no JS execution is needed to read it. The individual event detail page sampled (zweiland) repeats the identical dateblock markup per performance date plus its own embedded pretix.eu ticket link and free-text ticket-price tiers. No JSON-LD, wp-json, ICS, Fourvenues, or Sanity signature exists anywhere, but the plain server-rendered HTML directly answers every required field, so this genuinely terminates the escalation ladder at Level 1.

Ticketing is embedded via pretix.eu (the venue's own first-party ticket shop integration, not a third-party listings aggregator).

start_date.notes: Each dateblock (Th27082026) states a complete, self-contained date including year -- present identically on both the list card and the detail page. source_record_id.notes: The event's own URL slug (e.g. 'zweiland', from /en/veranstaltungen/zweiland/) is a stable, source-authored permalink for the PRODUCTION, but one production genuinely has multiple performance dates/times on the same page (observed: 6 dateblocks for Zweiland alone) -- so the slug alone is not unique per performance occurrence. A recommended, not-yet-empirically-verified strategy for a future collector: a compound id of {slug}+{ISO date+time from that occurrence's own dateblock}, since both halves are retained, source-authored facts on the same page. Left PARTIAL rather than promoted to PROVEN/DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT because collision-safety of that compound key has not been empirically stress-tested against real bulk data in this investigation.

blockers.description: A single production/slug can carry multiple performance dates/times (a real one-to-many relationship), so a collector must emit one Observation per dateblock, not one per slug/page, and needs a real source_record_id strategy (see field_assessment.source_record_id notes) rather than reusing the slug alone.
